A Unitree factory visit highlights the continuing role of manual assembly

Josef Chen describes the Hangzhou factory and why parts costs and changing designs affect automation economics.

Humanoids Daily ↗7 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

Observations from the visit

KAIKAKU founder Josef Chen published his account on November 5 after visiting Unitree in Hangzhou. He described one or two new automated actuator lines alongside workers operating winding machines. He did not establish the share of motors made automatically, and photography was prohibited on the production floor.

Historical costs provide context

The analysis cites 2025 company figures putting direct labor at roughly 8% of production cost, with materials accounting for most of the total. Halving labor therefore would not halve robot costs. These figures are historical context, not newly announced weekly financial results.

Limits of the account

Chen argues that frequent design changes complicate investment in dedicated machinery. His account combines a visit with entrepreneurial and investor commentary, rather than a comprehensive independent factory audit. The article image comes from an earlier assembly demonstration, not this visit.
